disclaimer: Operational observations only. Nothing on this page constitutes investment advice, a trading recommendation, or a securities opinion. Surprise probabilities reflect estimated likelihood of material deviation from analyst consensus on operational metrics — they are not price targets, fair value estimates, or buy/sell/hold signals.

entries.subject: Vestas Wind Systems A/S

stage2.note: Revenue beat of +5.96% vs consensus (EUR 3,966M vs EUR 3,743M). Predicted miss bias did not materialize. Three of four assumption-level mismatches were directionally incorrect; only IR-VWS-02 (Group EBIT margin >= 6.0%) was technically correct in absolute terms but conceptually misclassified as a Q1 driver rather than a full-year guidance check. Share price reaction approximately -1.5% intraday on report day, driven by negative free cash flow and high pre-earnings expectation bar — not by an operational miss. The Stage 2 'signal' label was incorrect; this was a calibration miss, not a calibrated noise call.

assumptions.name: Power Solutions demand trajectory
assumptions.testable_question: Q1 order intake >= EUR 3.9B (at least Q1/2025 level)?
assumptions.mismatch_drivers: US policy/tariff uncertainty, offshore FID weakness, 2025 order intake already declining YoY with falling ASP.
assumptions.actual_value: EUR 5.2B order intake (4,504 MW, +44% YoY in MW terms)
assumptions.miss_reason: Q1 2026 marked a clear cycle inflection: strong offshore order intake from UK, Germany, and South Korea reversed the 2025 declining trend. Stage 1 used 2025 trajectory data without applying a peer trajectory check, missing the trend break.

assumptions.name: Geopolitical/tariff stability for margins
assumptions.testable_question: Q1 Group EBIT margin before special items >= 6.0%?
assumptions.mismatch_drivers: Report explicitly names tariffs, trade barriers, sanctions as margin risk. Management assumes no significant deterioration — a high stability bar.
assumptions.actual_value: 3.2% Group EBIT margin before special items (best Q1 since 2018)
assumptions.miss_reason: Threshold of 6.0% formally missed (3.2% < 6.0%), but the testable question conflated full-year guidance (6-8%) with a Q1 hurdle. Q1 is structurally Vestas' weakest quarter due to delivery seasonality. FY guidance was maintained at 6-8%, and 3.2% was explicitly described by management as the best Q1 margin since 2018. driver_timing should have been full_year_impact, not current_quarter_impact. No directional Q1 miss occurred.

assumptions.name: Grid/permitting conversion stability
assumptions.mismatch_drivers: Outlook names lack of grid connections as risk. Revenue recognition only at control transfer. Market design and permitting remain bottlenecks.
assumptions.miss_reason: Revenue cleared the threshold by EUR 498M. Driven by offshore deliveries (812 MW vs 263 MW prior year, +209%) and improved manufacturing ramp. Stage 1 read forward-looking risk language in the 2025 Annual Report Outlook as base-case Q1 forecasting input, conflating risk-disclosure language with operational headwinds materializing in the reported quarter.

assumptions.name: Service segment weather/FX resilience
assumptions.testable_question: Q1 Service EBIT margin before special items >= 15.5%?
assumptions.actual_value: 16.3% Service EBIT margin before special items
assumptions.resolution_note: Service margin of 16.3% cleared the 15.5% threshold despite a 9.2% revenue decline in the segment (lower contract activity in EMEA). Margin discipline of the recovery plan validated. Aligned-call value confirmed.

overlap_clusters.shared_driver: Deterioration of external business conditions — policy/tariff uncertainty, permitting/grid frictions, and resulting delays in orders, handover, and margins.

lessons_learned: Three of four Stage 1 mismatches were directionally incorrect. The shared root cause across IR-VWS-01, IR-VWS-02, and IR-VWS-03 is that 2025-cycle priors and forward-looking outlook risk language were used as Q1 base-case inputs without recency or trajectory adjustment. The cycle inflected in the weeks before the report (offshore acceleration in UK, Germany, South Korea), and the Stage 1 evidence base did not capture this turn.

IR-VWS-02 illustrates a driver_timing classification error: the 6.0% Group EBIT margin question was framed as a Q1 hurdle but is structurally a full-year guidance check. Q1 is seasonally Vestas' weakest quarter; the 6.0% threshold is a full-year midpoint, not a quarterly base case. driver_timing should have been full_year_impact, with FY guidance reaffirmation as the relevant resolution test. FY guidance was maintained at 6-8% and Q1 margin was the best Q1 since 2018.

IR-VWS-03 illustrates a risk-language vs. base-case-forecast confusion: outlook risk disclosures (grid connection bottlenecks, permitting frictions) were read as operational forecasts for the reported quarter. Risk language in annual reports describes potential headwinds — it is not a probability-weighted Q1 forecast. Future analyses must distinguish risk-disclosure language from base-case operational guidance.

IR-VWS-01 illustrates a missed peer trajectory check: 2025 order intake decline data were structurally adjacent_cycle relative to Q1 2026, and the offshore order recovery was visible in Q4 2025 / early Q1 2026 peer activity. The peer trajectory (improving) was not applied. This case validates the v2.3.0 peer trajectory check as a necessary protocol element.

Calibration outcome: Stage 2 issued a 'signal' label at 35% surprise probability with miss bias. Reality was a +5.96% revenue beat with FY guidance maintained and order intake at a record EUR 5.2B. This is a directional miss with high confidence — the most damaging type of calibration error. The share price moved approximately -1.5% intraday, but driven by negative free cash flow and pre-earnings expectation bar (stock +13% YTD into print, +102% over twelve months), not by an operational miss. The 'right direction for the wrong reason' pattern is methodologically more concerning than a clean directional error.

The case has been formally documented as motivating evidence for the v2.3.0 / Stage 4 v1.1.0 protocol revision, specifically: (a) Peer Trajectory Check as a hard requirement for adjacent_cycle evidence, (b) driver_timing discipline distinguishing current_quarter_impact from full_year_impact, (c) Forward Guidance Coverage Rule treating FY guidance reaffirmation as a separate Stage 4 reaction layer rather than a Stage 3 input, and (d) explicit separation between outlook risk-disclosure language and base-case operational forecasts.

Public-facing implication: this case will be retained in the resolved log as a documented calibration miss. Future quarterly notes should include a 'reasoning audit' field distinguishing 'direction correct with correct reasoning' from 'direction correct by accident' to prevent post-hoc self-validation when share price coincidentally aligns with a flawed call.

score_summary.stage2_note: Stage 2 issued a 'signal' (35% surprise probability, miss bias) that did not materialize. Revenue beat consensus by +5.96%, order intake reached a record EUR 5.2B (+44% YoY in MW), FY guidance of EUR 20-22B and 6-8% EBIT margin was maintained, and a new EUR 100M share buy-back was initiated. Three of four Stage 1 assumption-level mismatches were directionally wrong; the fourth (IR-VWS-02) was a driver_timing classification error. The share price reaction (approximately -1.5% intraday) was driven by negative free cash flow and a high expectation bar after a strong YTD/12M run, not by an operational miss. Net: directional miss at Stage 2 with material calibration damage. The case is the empirical anchor for the v2.3.0 / Stage 4 v1.1.0 protocol revision.

entries.subject: Shopify Inc.

stage2.note: Consensus of $0.33 was an adjusted EPS estimate. Adjusted EPS came in at $0.36, beating by approximately 9%. GAAP EPS was -$0.45 due to a $1.08B net loss on equity and equity-method investments (non-operating, non-cash mark-to-market on minority stakes), but this is not directly comparable to the adjusted consensus. On the like-for-like adjusted basis, Shopify beat the $0.33 consensus, contradicting the predicted miss bias. The share price fell approximately -8.7% pre-market on the day of the report, but the cause was Q2 operating profit guidance below analyst expectations and rising transaction/loan loss reserves — not the trade/tariff friction thesis from IR-SHOP-02. Direction of share price reaction coincidentally aligned with the Stage 2 miss prediction, but for entirely different reasons. This is a 'right direction, wrong reasoning' case rather than a calibrated signal.

assumptions.name: Merchant demand sustainability
assumptions.resolution_note: Strongest quarterly revenue growth in over four years. Broad-based across geographies (North America, Europe, Asia Pacific) and merchant sizes. Aligned-call value confirmed.

assumptions.name: Trade/tariff friction on gross profit
assumptions.testable_question: Q1/2026 gross profit dollar growth >= 28% YoY?
assumptions.mismatch_drivers: De-minimis duty-free suspension continued Feb 2026. Cross-border friction rising for smaller merchants. Shopify names trade measures including tariffs as explicit risk factor.
assumptions.actual_value: +32.2% YoY gross profit growth ($1,546M vs $1,169M Q1/2025)
assumptions.miss_reason: Gross profit cleared the 28% threshold by 4.2 percentage points. The de-minimis and cross-border tariff thesis did not materialize as a Q1 gross profit headwind. Merchant solutions revenue grew 39% YoY (gross profit margin 39%), Shopify Payments penetration rose to 67%, and broad-based merchant demand offset any cross-border friction at the Q1 aggregate level. Risk-disclosure language about tariffs in 10-K/risk factors was misread as a base-case Q1 forecast input — the same pattern as IR-VWS-03.

assumptions.name: FX impact on reported growth
assumptions.actual_value: +34.3% YoY revenue growth (same threshold as IR-SHOP-01)
assumptions.resolution_note: FX did not produce a material headwind to reported growth. Aligned-call confirmed. Note: IR-SHOP-01 and IR-SHOP-03 share the same testable question, which is methodologically suboptimal — both assumptions resolve identically by construction. Future analyses should ensure each assumption has an independent testable question.

lessons_learned: IR-SHOP-02 repeated the same 'risk-disclosure language as base-case forecast' error documented in the Vestas IR-VWS-03 case. Shopify's 10-K listed trade measures and tariffs as risk factors, and de-minimis policy changes were a real macro datapoint. But these were not Q1 gross profit headwinds at the aggregate level. The 28% gross profit growth threshold was cleared by 4.2pp. Future analyses must distinguish risk-factor disclosures (legally required forward-looking risk language) from operational base-case forecasts.

Two of three testable questions (IR-SHOP-01 and IR-SHOP-03) shared an identical threshold (revenue growth >= 30% YoY). This is a methodological weakness: assumptions should resolve to independent operational questions to avoid double-counting alignment in score_summary. Future analyses must enforce one-question-per-assumption uniqueness as a Stage 1 hard rule.

Stage 2 issued a 'signal' label at 40% surprise probability with miss bias on adjusted EPS. Reality on the like-for-like adjusted basis was a +9.1% beat ($0.36 vs $0.33 consensus). This is a directional miss at Stage 2 with a 'signal' confidence claim — the same severity pattern as the Vestas case, though smaller in magnitude.

The share price moved approximately -8.7% pre-market in the predicted direction, but caused by factors entirely outside the Stage 1 thesis: Q2 operating profit guidance below analyst expectations, rising transaction and loan loss reserves, and a $1.08B GAAP equity-investment writedown (non-operating). The Stage 1 trade/tariff thesis (IR-SHOP-02) had no causal link to the realized price move. This is the 'right direction, wrong reasoning' pattern flagged in the Vestas case — methodologically more concerning than a clean directional miss because it invites post-hoc self-validation.

The Q2 operating profit guidance miss was the actual primary market reaction driver — a forward-guidance signal that Stage 1 / Stage 2 in the v2.2.0 protocol did not score because Forward Guidance was not yet a mandatory Stage 1 assumption category. Under v2.3.0 / Stage 4 v1.1.0, this case would have triggered the Forward Guidance Coverage Rule and required a separate Stage 4 forward-guidance assumption with next_quarter_guidance reaction_driver_type. The case validates the v2.3.0 architecture revision.

GAAP/adjusted distinction created additional resolution complexity: GAAP EPS of -$0.45 (driven by a $1.08B mark-to-market loss on minority equity investments) is not comparable to the adjusted $0.33 consensus. Future analyses must explicitly state whether the consensus_eps anchor is GAAP or adjusted, and the resolution must use the matching basis. For Shopify and similar companies with material non-operating equity holdings, adjusted EPS is the operationally relevant anchor.

Public-facing implication: Shopify is the second consecutive case (after Vestas) where the share price moved coincidentally in the predicted direction but for reasons unrelated to the Stage 1 thesis. This pattern strengthens the case for a 'reasoning audit' field in future quarterly notes that explicitly distinguishes 'direction correct with correct reasoning' from 'direction correct by accident'. Without this distinction, two consecutive 'right-direction-wrong-reasoning' cases would falsely register as calibration successes in any aggregate hit-rate statistic.

score_summary.stage2_note: Stage 2 issued a 'signal' (40% surprise probability, miss bias) on adjusted EPS. Adjusted EPS came in at $0.36 vs $0.33 consensus, a +9.1% beat — directionally opposite to the prediction. The share price fell approximately -8.7% pre-market, but driven by Q2 operating profit guidance and rising transaction/loan loss reserves, not by the IR-SHOP-02 trade/tariff thesis. Two of three assumption-level calls were correct (IR-SHOP-01 and IR-SHOP-03 both confirmed), but they shared an identical testable question (methodological weakness). The single Stage 1 mismatch (IR-SHOP-02) was directionally wrong; gross profit grew 32.2% YoY, clearing the 28% threshold by 4.2pp. Net: directional miss at Stage 2 on the operational EPS basis with the right share-price direction for the wrong reason — the 'right direction by accident' pattern documented in the Vestas case applies here as well.

entries.subject: GE Vernova Inc.

stage2.note: GAAP EPS of $17.44 includes $3.99B pre-tax gain from Prolec GE remeasurement and $330M from Proficy divestiture (non-operating, non-recurring). Adjusted EPS reconstructed from Adjusted EBITDA of $896M, D&A of $341M, non-operating benefit income of $134M, and 272M diluted shares yields approximately $1.97–$2.16 depending on effective tax rate assumption (midpoint ~$2.06). Beat of roughly 15% vs $1.79 consensus. Self-labeled 'noise' at 45% probability — system correctly refrained from claiming a strong signal.

assumptions.name: Gas Power demand trajectory
assumptions.condition_met_note: Below threshold by $29M (0.6%) — de minimis deviation, materially aligned with 'no mismatch' call.

assumptions.name: Wind segment loss trajectory
assumptions.testable_question: Wind segment EBITDA better than -$150M in Q1?
assumptions.mismatch_drivers: BOEM suspended Vineyard Wind, Revolution Wind, Sunrise Wind. Weak onshore orders from US policy uncertainty. Tariff impact $300-400M guided for full year.
assumptions.magnitude_note: Actual result $232M worse than threshold and $218M worse than guided full-year Wind loss of roughly -$400M after just one quarter — deterioration substantially more severe than anticipated.

lessons_learned: Stage 1 correctly resolved all three assumption calls — two aligned (Power marginally below threshold but de minimis; Electrification clearly above), one material mismatch (Wind) confirmed with severity exceeding expectation.
Wind mismatch validates the Tetlock-style edge-seeking approach: the analysis identified a blind spot in consensus guidance and was directionally correct with meaningful magnitude.

Stage 2 miss on direction was correctly self-labeled 'noise' at 45% probability — confidence calibration held. The Prolec-GE remeasurement gain of $3.99B was a bookkeeping event not foreseeable at analysis time and does not materially affect Adjusted EPS comparison.

GAAP vs. Adjusted EPS distinction is critical for resolution: headline GAAP of $17.44 would falsely suggest a 874% beat; reconstructed Adjusted EPS of ~$2.00 shows a more modest 10–20% beat vs consensus.

entries.subject: onsemi (ON Semiconductor Corporation)

stage2.note: Non-GAAP diluted EPS $0.64 vs consensus $0.62 — beat of approximately 3.2%, well within the consensus spread of $0.59–$0.66. Group revenue of $1,513M came in above the guidance midpoint of $1,485M; Non-GAAP gross margin landed at 38.5%. Self-labeled 'noise' at 45% probability with a gap of only 5pp from neutral — system correctly refrained from claiming a directional signal. The marginal beat in the opposite direction is consistent with calibrated uncertainty on a noise-classified call.

assumptions.name: Automotive demand stability
assumptions.resolution_note: onsemi reorganised reporting segments to PSG/AMG/ISG; Automotive end-market revenue is no longer disclosed as a standalone figure. AMG (which contains automotive analog and mixed-signal exposure) reported $540M, down 3% QoQ. Management qualitatively cited 900V EV architecture wins with Geely and NIO and continued Treo-based design momentum, with no indication of automotive demand deterioration. Aligned-call cannot be formally resolved against the original threshold but qualitative evidence is consistent with the original verdict.

assumptions.name: Industrial stabilisation
assumptions.mismatch_drivers: Infineon Core Industrial GIP -21% sequentially, flat recovery only. ST Industrial still declining in FY25. PMI >50 but decelerating. Microchip and NXP show mixed signals. External evidence points to shallow, uneven industrial recovery insufficient to support near-stable Industrial revenue.
assumptions.actual_value: Not separately reported (segment restructuring); group revenue $1,513M above midpoint, Q2 guidance raised to $1,535–1,635M
assumptions.miss_reason: The material_mismatch could not be formally resolved against the original threshold because onsemi reorganised reporting into PSG/AMG/ISG and no longer discloses Industrial end-market revenue separately. However, the directional thesis (industrial weakness pressuring guidance) was not supported by the broader picture: group revenue exceeded the guidance midpoint, Non-GAAP gross margin came in at 38.5%, AI Data Center revenue more than doubled YoY and grew 30%+ sequentially, Q2 guidance was raised, and management explicitly stated 'demand strengthened through the quarter and we have moved beyond the cyclical trough on a path to recovery.' New design wins in industrial energy storage (Sineng 430kW) further suggest constructive end-market dynamics. The mismatch direction (guidance_too_optimistic) is contradicted by the available qualitative and group-level evidence.

assumptions.name: AI/Data Center mix supporting gross margin
assumptions.resolution_note: Non-GAAP gross margin of 38.5% cleared the 38.0% threshold by 50bp. AI Data Center revenue more than doubled YoY and grew 30%+ sequentially, validating the AI/Data Center mix thesis as a margin support factor. Q2 guidance of 38.0–40.0% non-GAAP gross margin signals continued sequential margin expansion.

lessons_learned: Stage 2 self-labeled 'noise' at 45% probability — the marginal 3.2% beat in the opposite direction is well within the calibrated uncertainty band of a noise classification. No methodology damage; system correctly avoided a false signal claim.

The Stage 1 IR-ON-02 material_mismatch was not confirmed at resolution. Diagnostic root cause: peer evidence base used in the analysis (Infineon Q1 FY26, ST Q4'25, NXP Q4'25, Microchip Q3 FY26) was structurally one quarter older than the resolution period. Cyclical recovery turn occurred in the intervening weeks, and aggregate-level peer pessimism overshadowed sub-segment recovery signals (Microchip 'broad-based recovery' language, NXP 'improving demand environment') that were present but underweighted in the F/I/S aggregation.

The case has been formally documented as the empirical basis for the v1.3.0 protocol patch (Peer Recency Classification and Peer Trajectory Check) and the v2.0.0 architecture revision (introduction of Stage 2 Challenge phase between assumption analysis and consensus scaling).

Segment reporting reorganisation (Auto/Industrial/Other → PSG/AMG/ISG) made two of three testable questions formally unresolvable against their original thresholds. Future analyses should flag announced segment restructurings ahead of the resolution period and adjust testable question framing accordingly.

Pipeline behaviour confirmed: the Stage 1 mismatch was directionally incorrect but Stage 2 (segment scaling and noise classification) prevented this from propagating to a public-facing signal. The dampening architecture worked as designed.

score_summary.stage2_note: Industrial segment share 28.9% scaled the -17pp assumption-level mismatch down to -4.9pp at group level, producing a 45% surprise probability classified as noise. Group EPS came in at $0.64 vs consensus $0.62 — a 3.2% beat that is directionally opposite to the predicted miss but within calibrated uncertainty for a noise-labeled call. The Stage 1 mismatch direction was not confirmed; the Stage 2 noise classification was correctly restrained. Net: directional miss at Stage 2 with no calibration damage; methodological lesson on peer evidence recency captured in lessons_learned.

entries.subject: ASML Holding NV

assumptions.name: Export control risk
assumptions.miss_reason: MATCH Act appeared April 2026, after quarter-end March 29. Driver had no mechanical impact on Q1 numbers.

lessons_learned: Generic cycle skepticism against a well-understood mega-trend (AI/EUV) rarely constitutes a genuine edge.
Timing mismatch between driver appearance and quarter-end is a fixable methodological error — now addressed by driver_timing field.
Two correct aligned-calls (IR-ASML-01, IR-ASML-02) confirm guidance robustness and have real value.
